threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: When you say 'the Tube' instead of 'the underground', you can spot the fresh faces immediately. It's like a secret handshake we just don’t have.
Last night on the 59, a guy was serenading a cat. The cat wasn’t having it, just stared him down. Classic Brixton vibes.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a couple arguing over the last slice of pizza at the Kottbusser Tor late one night, only to see them sharing the next one in a park.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a guy selling currywurst with one hand while juggling beer bottles with the other—pure Kreuzberg chaos.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot 'locals' by their nonchalance at BART delays; they’ve already abandoned plans and are just grabbing a taco instead.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the Muni last week, it stopped for a pigeon that clearly had priorities. Only in this city do the birds halt transit!

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all tapas come with an olive for a garnish. In Gràcia, it's usually a good slice of tomato or a patata brava instead.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewildered expressions while trying to negotiate the intricacies of the metro map—it's almost as if they expect it to make sense.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the tube' instead of just saying 'the train' like everyone else does around here.
Last week on the N37, a guy tried to sell his mixtape. Not sure if it was bravado or just the cold, but he performed a whole track without a microphone!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The day I heard a spontaneous jam session outside my window, mixing Turkish folk with techno beats. Neukölln in a nutshell.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a packed club where people dance surrounded by cages filled with live chickens. It’s as bizarre as it sounds.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their effortless dodging of the BART delays; tourists just stand there, eyes wide, confused by the frenzy.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught a glimpse of a whole marching band stuck at Civic Center, waiting for the Muni to clear. Only in SF do musicians become part of the transit chaos.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all bars in Gràcia close at midnight, but locals know the best ones keep it going until 2 or 3, especially on weekends.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by the way they still think they can catch a train during a Rodalies strike, frantically checking their phones for updates.
